catalysts.headline: IREN fell 11.19% to $26.99, a new 52-week low, amid investor concern over how the company will fund its AI-data-center buildout, after Morningstar revised its view on IREN citing rising borrowing costs
IREN fell 6.27% to $38.69; coverage cited AI Cloud revenue reaching $128.8M versus $16.4M in fiscal 2025, though the exact period this figure covers was not independently established this session
catalysts.note: AI Cloud revenue figure's period is ambiguous — IREN's own Q4 FY2026 (ended 2026-06-30) AI Cloud revenue was reported as $70.5M, so $128.8M would represent either a later, unreported period or a different revenue scope; not reconciled with figures already on file.

catalysts.headline: Q4 FY2026: revenue $137.2M (down from $144.8M in Q3, missed ~$157.1M consensus); net loss $684.0M incl. $450.4M in asset impairments; AI Cloud revenue grew sequentially from $33.6M to $70.5M (+110% QoQ), now over half of quarterly revenue; adjusted EBITDA $19.2M (~53% below expectations). FY2026 full year: revenue $707.0M (up from $501.0M), net loss $702.6M vs FY2025 net income $86.9M. Guided FY2027 capex of $25B-$30B, with roughly $8B of funding still needed.

notes: IREN shares fell sharply through mid-October 2026 (from the low-to-mid $40s into the high $20s) amid financing-cost concerns tied to its AI-cloud capex buildout (FY2027 capex guided at $25B-$30B, already on file).
